headline: Kai, futures point higher after the worst day since June — Apple reports tonight, and the midterms are tomorrow.
subline: The AI rout that just erased $5 trillion gets its rebound attempt, Doha talks are easing oil off its spike, and October payrolls land Friday.
asof: Pre-market · futures and overnight quotes as of ~6:40 AM ET · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Futures rise after the AI sell-off
items.sentence: S&P 500 futures are up 0.53%, Nasdaq-100 futures 0.86% and Dow futures 0.58% after an AI-fueled rout that briefly pushed the Nasdaq 100 into correction, per Yahoo Finance's live blog.

items.title: Worst day since June for the S&P 500
items.sentence: Friday's 1.82% slide left the index at 7,580.07, its worst session since June, with Intel and Amazon deepening the AI sell-off, per BBN Times.

items.title: Apple and Palantir report after the bell
items.sentence: Apple (consensus EPS of $1.98) and Palantir ($0.33) post results after today's close, October ISM manufacturing lands at 10 a.m. ET, and Friday's payrolls consensus sits at 55,000 after September's 29,000, per Gotrade's week-ahead.

items.title: Oil slides on Doha talks; gold steadies
items.sentence: Brent's January contract trades near $110, down 3% from above $114 on Friday, as talks to end the US-Iran war continue, while gold holds near $3,915 after Friday's one-year low, per Saxo Bank.

items.title: Bitcoin holds near $78,000 after Binance hack
items.sentence: The $6.3 billion Binance breach knocked bitcoin toward $76,000 and October closed down more than 7%, but it trades near $78,000 as withdrawals resume and spot-ETF outflows hit $643 million on October 30, per crypto.news.

items.title: Midterms tomorrow: Congress on the ballot
items.sentence: Voters decide control of the House and Senate on Tuesday, and NPR's election-night guide maps poll-closing times by state and the races that will tell the story early.

items.title: Trump: Iran war ends 'one way or the other'
items.sentence: Negotiators met in Doha for a third day of talks to end the US-Iran war, and Trump said the conflict will be put away very soon, 'one way or the other,' per CBS News.

items.title: Kherson ceasefire expires; civilians evacuated
items.sentence: Ukraine evacuated civilians from parts of the Kherson region as the Oleshky humanitarian ceasefire ran out, with Russia declining to extend the pause, per AP reporting carried by US News.

items.title: Halevi: October 7 was preventable
items.sentence: Former IDF chief Herzi Halevi said the October 7 attack was preventable while insisting there was 'absolutely no internal betrayal,' per The Times of Israel's liveblog.

items.title: China factory gauge slips back into contraction
items.sentence: China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October from 50.1 in September, back below the line dividing growth from contraction, per Saxo Bank's morning rundown.

items.title: Data-center pause backers eye 15 governorships
items.sentence: Candidates backing a pause on new data centers could win up to 15 of the 36 governor races on Tuesday's ballot, per an analysis by The Information cited in AI Weekly.

items.title: OpenAI trims its raise to $20 billion
items.sentence: OpenAI is now seeking about $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, down from $30 billion at $1.4 trillion, per a Financial Times report relayed by AI Weekly.

items.title: AI borrowing hits $466 billion; Meta outlook cut
items.sentence: AI-linked companies have raised $466 billion of debt this year against $101 billion in the same period of 2025, and S&P cut Meta's credit outlook to negative, per Wall Street Journal and CNBC reporting collected by AI Weekly.

items.title: AMD undercuts Nvidia on inference cost
items.sentence: A SemiAnalysis test served the Kimi K3 model at $0.15 per million tokens on AMD's MI355X against $0.22 on Nvidia's GB200 racks, a day before AMD reports earnings, per AI Weekly.

items.title: Trojanized Claude Code extension hit Cursor
items.sentence: A tampered version of the Claude Code extension sat in Cursor's marketplace for about 11 hours, exposing up to 5,000 developers before a clean build shipped, per The Hacker News via AI Weekly.
